rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Playing Turns 2 Covering icons 3 Achievements 4 End of game 5 Pit variant 6 Mini Expansion: Souvenir Shops Playing Turns To start: Place your initial tile on your park area. (It must fit on the board and not cover a pit.) In later turns, you may place exactly one tile from your supply in your park. Even if you have more than one tile in your supply, you may only place one per turn. The new tile must be touching at least one edge of a previously placed tile. It must fit fully on the board, not overlap another tile and not cover a pit. If you do not have any tiles, you must pass. After passing, you must take a Green Area of your choice, and then end your turn. Covering icons When any portion of a tile covers an icon on the park board, you get a reward from the group supply. Icon Effect Green wheelbarrow Gain a Green Area (1 to 3 squares) of your choice. White cement truck Gain an Animal House tile (4 squares) or a Green Area (1 to 3 squares) to your supply. Animal Houses earn victory points when placed. Orange excavator Gain an Enclosure tile (5 squares) or an Animal House tile (4 squares) or a Green Area (1 to 3 squares) to your supply. Enclosures earn victory points when placed. Construction crew Gain a new park area and place it immediately. It must border an existing area and not be at a level lower than your entrance. When you fill any park area completely, you earn a bear statue worth victory points. Finishing a park area earlier is worth more victory points. Achievements Most experienced Bärenpark players like to play with achievements. 3 random achievements are placed under the supply area. Hover over the achievements to see what is required to earn them. (Long press on mobile). Completing achievements earlier is worth more victory points. End of game The game end is triggered when a player completes all four of their Park Areas. Each other player gets one more turn and then counts up their points. The player with the most points wins. In case of a tie, the tied players total the point values on the tiles left in their supply (which they did not place)-the highest-value total breaks the tie. If still tied, there are multiple winners. Pit variant As an expert variant, you can cover up pits on your last turn, though you won't get the bear bonus for a tile with its pit covered up. Mini Expansion: Souvenir Shops When you cover the construction crew icon on your final (i.e., fourth) park area, immediately choose an available souvenir shop tile and place it in your supply. (The larger the tile you choose, the fewer points you will get for it once placed.)

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Play mainly 2 player and Patchwork is a much better design.  For more than two play Parade, Biblios, Arboretum for a much more satisfying experience

[Rating: 1/10] Player 1 wins.  That's the true title of the game. In fact, player 1 will only kiss if they screw up. Player 2 can only win if player 1 lets them due to playing poorly.  Due to the way scoring works the first player gets first choice of tiles, and the first player will fill their board first, and so get statues first, which are worth more points.  "Play with achievements" except they are also points for the first person, so played one gets first choice there too.  Play almost any other tile placement game, there's nothing positive to this one except the theming.

[Rating: 2/10] Classic example of the 'polyomino' fad which ran rampant through the gaming world in 2016-2019. Having this tetris-style mini-game as a large part of a design inevitably means a focus on player-board puzzling over meaningful player interaction, and this was no exception. Pretty forgettable.

[Rating: 2/10] It's about as much as one can expect out of a family-weight polyomino MPS excursion. It's inoffensive, but uncompelling.

[Rating: 2/10] Hot garbage. Buy it if you like light games or are playing with newer gamers. I bounced off of this like a ping pong ball.   I read the rules and said where are the game mechanics. Then I played a round. Yup, called it.

[Rating: 2/10] Not a game, but a puzzle you can play yourself. I consider games to be based on interaction with others, not people just sitting in the corner doing their own thing. This is basically just a race to see who can make a better puzzle first.  If you like solitaire board games with NO player interaction you may like Barenpark. If you are like me, and prefer games with player interaction look elsewhere.  A lot of people like this game, but I'm not sure why as it's boring and unengaging.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Drab polyomino tile layer, with the only real point of interest being the race for limited tiles. Uninspired.

[Rating: 3/10] :star::star::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Decent tile-laying game about building a bear park. There is enough decision space to make the game interesting. There's the nice trade-off of finishing a square or to cover more icons to get the high scoring tiles.  Setup is a big pain  Always play with the achievements though.
